Draft · national view

Where America's tap water comes from

Every county's community water systems, from EPA's drinking water records. Pick a layer, or find your county. About 29% of people on community systems get groundwater from wells, and 21% of small systems (under 500 people) had a health-based violation in the last five years.

Hover or tap a county for details.

Community water systems only (year-round systems like city utilities), as of EPA's November 2026 download. Each system is counted in one home county. Violation rates need at least 5 small systems in a county (1,343 counties qualify); the rest are left blank. Tribal systems are regulated by EPA and tied to tribal lands rather than counties, so they are compared by region below.

What stands out

Where you live matters more than anything else in the data. Among small systems, the share with a recent health-based violation runs from OK 70%, NM 60%, AZ 47% down to GA 3%, HI 5%, IA 5%. Minnesota is 10%, 14th lowest of 49 states. A gap that wide is mostly about state rules, testing and reporting, not just water.

Surface water systems get more violations than well systems, at every size. 24% of systems that draw from rivers and lakes had one in the last five years, vs. 19% of well systems. Surface water needs more treatment, and every treatment step is another rule to break.

Tribal systems, region by region

In Minnesota, small tribal systems had about 3.5x the violation rate of similar state systems. Nationally the gap is about 1.8x (126 of 342 tribal systems, 37%, vs. 21% of state systems in the same regions), and it depends on where you look.
